thread:
alex.support: Docly reporting repeated 504s from the hosted API since ~14:05 UTC. Happens on text-gen streaming calls, p95 timeouts ~30s. Sample request id: req-8f3c. Customer says spike started after a campaign. @jen.oncall can you pick this up?

jen.oncall: On it. Can you paste tenant id + a repro curl? Also any immediate mitigations the support team tried?

alex.support: tenant: docly-prod-77. Repro curl they used:```curl -X POST \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"longform-2","input":"Summarize this...","stream":true}'```They tried retrying but still get 504s and occasional 500s.

mike.eng: I'm seeing matching errors in gateway logs: `504 gateway timeout -> backend timeout` Batch logs show enqueues greatly exceeding queue depth. Snapshot: `continuous-batcher.queue_length=6124` `queue_depth_limit=5000` `dequeue_p95=18.3s` `backend_fill_rate=0.7` Also evidence of KV cache warmups causing long first-token latencies.

jen.oncall: That queue length is nasty. Can we temporarily disable continuous batching for this tenant or route them to a less-congested pool?

mike.eng: We can apply a tenant override. Trying to disable batching for docly-prod-77 and apply a soft throttle. Running admin command: `adminctl tenant override --tenant docly-prod-77 --disable-batching true --burst-limit 50`

ops-bot: run: `adminctl tenant override --tenant docly-prod-77 --disable-batching true --burst-limit 50` -> SUCCESS (1732104728)

sara.ml: Heads-up: disabling batching will raise per-token cost but should reduce tail timeouts since requests won't block behind long queues. Also recommend fallback to `small-lm-v1` for non-critical routes while we drain the backlog.

mike.eng: Throttle + disable applied. Watching metrics: `continuous-batcher.queue_length` fell from 6124 -> 1189 in 35s, `dequeue_p95` down to ~1.8s. Gateway 504s dropped in our sampling. Pushed a temporary route to `small-lm-v1` for non-stream calls.

liaison.docly: Docly confirms 504s dropped dramatically. Their engineers see success rate improve from ~78% -> 99% on previously failing requests. Thanks.

jen.oncall: Quick post-incident notes (to share with CS): probable root cause = sudden request fanout from marketing + long KV cache warmups (cold shards) -> continuous-batcher backlog past queue_depth_limit -> tail timeouts and 5xx. Mitigations applied: tenant-level batching disable + burst throttle + model fallback.

mike.eng: Filed infra tasks: INF-1982 \"kvcache warmup & prefetch for high-fanout tenants\", INF-1983 \"per-tenant soft queue depth & early-reject policy (informative 429)\". Also adding a runbook step: when queue_length > 4k and p95_dequeue > 10s, consider per-tenant disable-batching + throttling before full-scale scaling.

alex.support: I'll keep monitoring and will close the escalation after 24h of stable metrics from the customer. Closing note: customer asked for more visibility into queue signals; add an endpoint to surface per-tenant queue depth to support UI.

jen.oncall: +1 to adding visibility. Action owners assigned in Slack thread. :thumbsup:

mike.eng: Leaving a short CLI snippet for reproducing local check:```python
# check queue length
resp = requests.get('https://infra.internal/api/queues?tenant=docly-prod-77')
print(resp.json())
```

alex.support: Thanks everyone. I'll update the CS ticket and ask Docly to notify if any regression.
